The [[1972 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the XX Olympiad, were a summer [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Munich]], West Germany, from 26 August through 11 September 1972.<ref>{{cite web |title=Munich 1972 Olympic Games {{!}} Athletes, Massacre, Facts, & Summer Olympics |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/Munich-1972-Olympic-Games |website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |access-date=3 January 2025 |language=en |date=11 December 2024 |archive-date=19 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240119230836/https://www.britannica.com/event/Munich-1972-Olympic-Games |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Olympedia">{{cite web |title=1972 Summer Olympics Overview |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/18 |website=[[Olympedia]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211190454/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/18 |archive-date=11 February 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=19 February 2025}}</ref> 7,134 athletes representing 121 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated,<ref name="munich">{{cite web |title=Munich 1972 Summer Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/munich-1972 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=2 January 2025 |archive-date=17 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211217150855/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/munich-1972 |url-status=live }}</ref> which included 11 teams making their debut at the Summer Olympics: [[Albania at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Albania]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Albania (ALB) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/ALB |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=18 February 2025 |archive-date=30 Benin),<ref>{{cite web |title=Benin (BEN) |url=http://olympedia.org/countries/BEN |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=18 February 2025 |archive-date=4 February 2025 |title=Timeline: When every Olympic sport made its debut |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/04/sport/olympic-sports-timeline-history-dg/index.html |website=[[CNN]] |date=4 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240813221315/https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/04/sport/olympic-sports-timeline-history-dg/index.html |archive-date=13 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Choi |first1=Annette |access-date=18 February 2025 |language=en}}</ref> [[Kayaking]], the [[canoe slalom]], and indoor [[handball]] all made their Olympic debuts, while [[archery]] returned to the Olympic program after a 52-year hiatus.<ref name="munich" />

[[Rhodesia at the Olympics|Rhodesia]] had been barred from participating at the [[1968 Summer Olympics|1968 Games]] due to racial policies and threats by athletes to boycott the event, but in 1971, the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) ruled that Rhodesia would be invited to compete at the 1972 Olympic Games.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chikamhi |first1=Eddie |title=ZOC, NAAZ pay tribute to Zimbabwe's Olympic pioneer Tseriwa |url=https://www.herald.co.zw/zoc-naaz-pay-tribute-to-zimbabwes-olympic-pioneer-tseriwa/ |website=[[The Herald (Zimbabwe)|The Herald]] |access-date=19 February 2025 |location=Zimbabwe |language=en |date=16 March 2023 |archive-date=4 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404095841/https://www.herald.co.zw/zoc-naaz-pay-tribute-to-zimbabwes-olympic-pioneer-tseriwa/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Two sprinters gave the black-power salute at the Olympics. It took them decades to recover from that gesture. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/two-sprinters-gave-the-black-power-salute-at-the-olympics-it-took-them-decades-to-recover-from-that-gesture/2018/05/28/b29e9dfc-4a58-11e8-827e-190efaf1f1ee_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=28 May 2018 |last1=Maese |first1=Rick |url-access=subscription |access-date=19 February 2025 |language=en |archive-date=31 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331141807/https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/two-sprinters-gave-the-black-power-salute-at-the-olympics-it-took-them-decades-to-recover-from-that-gesture/2018/05/28/b29e9dfc-4a58-11e8-827e-190efaf1f1ee_story.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Rhodesia, Barred in '68, Invited to '72 Olympics |url=http://nytimes.com/1971/03/29/archives/rhodesia-barred-in-68-invited-to-72-olympics.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=29 March 1971 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219201743/https://www.nytimes.com/1971/03/29/archives/rhodesia-barred-in-68-invited-to-72-olympics.html |archive-date=19 February 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=19 February 2025 |page=45}}</ref> Athletes from other African nations protested this invitation and again threatened to boycott the games over those policies. Four days before the opening ceremonies, the IOC voted to rescind their invitation and exclude the Rhodesian athletes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympics Boycott? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1972/08/22/archives/olympics-boycott.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=1972-08-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317160942/https://www.nytimes.com/1972/08/22/archives/olympics-boycott.html |archive-date=2025-03-17 |url-status=live |access-date=19 February 2025 |page=42}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Amdur |first=Neil |date=23 August 1972 |title=Rhodesia Out of Olympics After a Dispute on Racism |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1972/08/23/archives/rhodesia-out-of-olympics-after-a-dispute-on-racism-rhodesia-is.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250102210021/https://www.nytimes.com/1972/08/23/archives/rhodesia-out-of-olympics-after-a-dispute-on-racism-rhodesia-is.html |archive-date=2 January 2025 |access-date=2 January 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]] |page=1}}</ref>

Athletes representing 48 NOCs received at least one medal, with 25 NOCs winning at least one gold medal.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> The [[Soviet Union at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Soviet Union]] won the most gold medals, with 50, and the most overall medals, with 99.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> North Korea and [[Uganda at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Uganda]] won their nations' first Summer Olympic gold medals, which was the first medal of any kind at the Summer Olympics for North Korea.<ref name="North Korea IOC" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Uganda – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/uganda |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226041952/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/uganda |archive-date=26 December 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=3 January 2025 }}</ref> [[Colombia at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Colombia]] and [[Niger at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Niger]] also won their nations' first Olympic medals of any kind.<ref>{{cite web |title=Colombia – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/colombia |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042827/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/colombia |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=3 January 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Niger – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/niger |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006043820/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/niger |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=3 January 2025}}</ref>

Among individual participants, American swimmer [[Mark Spitz]] won the most medals at the games with seven, all of which were gold.<ref>{{cite web |title=1972 Munich Summer Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=3 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417040848/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ |archive-date=17 April 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Spitz also became the record holder for [[List of multiple Olympic gold medalists at a single Games|most gold medals at a single Olympic Games]], a record that stood for 36 years until American swimmer [[Michael Phelps]] surpassed that mark with eight gold medals at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Phelps: The man who dominated the Olympic pool like no other |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/michael-phelps-olympic-medals-record-how-many-gold-swimmer-world-record |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=5 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926103755/https://olympics.com/en/news/michael-phelps-olympic-medals-record-how-many-gold-swimmer-world-record |archive-date=26 September 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Venkat |first1=Rahul |access-date=3 January 2025}}</ref>

==Medal table==

The medal table is based on information provided by the IOC and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>

At the 1972 Games, events in [[Boxing at the 1980 Summer Olympics|boxing]] resulted in bronze medals being awarded to each of the competitors who lost their semi-final matches, as opposed to them taking part in a [[Third place playoff|third place tiebreaker]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Explained: Two bronze medals are awarded in the Olympics boxing competition |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=1 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328143327/https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |archive-date=28 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Ansari |first1=Aarish |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref> Events in [[Judo at the 1980 Summer Olympics|judo]] used a [[repechage system]], which also resulted in two bronze medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Repechage in wrestling and other sports explained – the second chance |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=21 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240802015913/https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |archive-date=2 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Nag |first1=Utathya |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref>

In the [[Gymnastics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Women's uneven bars|women's uneven bars]], there was a two-way tie for second, resulting in two silver medals being issued and no bronze medal being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Munich 1972 uneven bars women Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/munich-1972/results/gymnastics-artistic/uneven-bars-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109134517/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/munich-1972/results/gymnastics-artistic/uneven-bars-women |archive-date=9 November 2022 |url-status=live |access-date=18 February 2025}}</ref> In [[Football at the 1972 Summer Olympics|men's football]], the third-place match ended in a tie, resulting in both teams receiving bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Football, Men |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/33855 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=18 February 2025 |archive-date=28 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228035556/https://www.olympedia.org/results/33855 |url-status=live }}</ref>

| align="left" | [[Jaime Huélamo]] was disqualified for doping violations.<ref name="NZ Herald 1">{{cite web |title=Cycling: Biddle's Olympic medal riddle |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/olympics/cycling-biddles-olympic-medal-riddle/LU6OX4Q23BP72PRDKO4FVRKL5M/ |website=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=7 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219202340/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/olympics/cycling-biddles-olympic-medal-riddle/LU6OX4Q23BP72PRDKO4FVRKL5M/ |archive-date=19 February 2025 |url-status=live |last1=Alderson |first1=Andrew |access-date=19 February 2025 |language=en-NZ}}</ref> New Zealand's [[Bruce Biddle]] finished fourth, but was not awarded the bronze due to stipulations that medal winners had to be drug tested.<ref name="NZ Herald 2">{{cite web |title=Olympics: Biddle's bid for bronze declined |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/olympics-biddles-bid-for-bronze-declined/RC2JJIZYPMODHVKTNP2PXVEML4/ |website=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=2 September 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219201856/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/olympics-biddles-bid-for-bronze-declined/RC2JJIZYPMODHVKTNP2PXVEML4/ |archive-date=19 February 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=19 February 2025 |language=en-NZ}}</ref> Biddle had tried to get tested following the race on the advice of his team's manager, in the event of a disqualification, but he was turned away.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bruce Biddle |url=https://olympic.org.nz/athletes/bruce-biddle |website=[[New Zealand Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214204816/https://olympic.org.nz/athletes/bruce-biddle |archive-date=14 February 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=19 February 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="NZ Herald 1" />

| rowspan="4" align="left" | [[Aad van den Hoek]] was disqualified for doping violations, causing the entire Dutch cycling team to lose their medals, as it was a team event.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 August 2004 |title=Cycling |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/cycling-xxwj5szlvcp |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219182915/https://www.thetimes.com/article/cycling-xxwj5szlvcp |archive-date=19 February 2025 |access-date=19 February 2025 |website=[[The Times]] |language=en}}</ref> The Belgian team finished fourth, but did not receive the bronze medals because they had not been subjected to drug testing, a requirement for medal winners at the time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cycling at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games: Men's 100 kilometres Team Time Trial |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/CYC/mens-100-kilometres-team-time-trial.html |website=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=19 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418020126/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/CYC/mens-100-kilometres-team-time-trial.html |archive-date=18 April 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="NZ Herald 2" />

| rowspan="4" align="left" | [[Rick DeMont]] was disqualified after testing positive for [[ephedrine]], a substance which was found in DeMont's asthma medication. DeMont had declared his asthma medication to the team, but the team had failed to clear it with the IOC, leading to his gold medal being stripped from him.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grohmann |first=Karolos |date=14 February 2022 |title=Olympic swimmer remembers his 1972 doping punishment |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/us-doping-blunder-munich-72-games-sent-me-dark-place-demont-2022-02-14/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519233936/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/us-doping-blunder-munich-72-games-sent-me-dark-place-demont-2022-02-14/ |archive-date=19 May 2022 |access-date=19 February 2025 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref name="DeMont">{{cite news |title=Better late than never |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/olympics/news/2001/01/30/usoc_demont_ap/ |date=30 January 2001 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010507004733/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/olympics/news/2001/01/30/usoc_demont_ap/ |archive-date=7 May 2001 |url-status=dead |work=[[CNN/SI]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>
